relations.label: related
relations.reason: Dark matter is made of bound states of a 'Dual' partner of every SM particle (S1). Winn's duality, though, is electric→magnetic charge, chromoelectric→chromomagnetic, L↔R and spin −½, with flavor and mass kept (S2). Nothing in the abstract, the 27 slides or the summary places the partners in the other polarization of phase space: every 'momentum' is angular momentum, momentum transfer or parity; 'space' never occurs; 'reciprocal' means Dirac's e·g relation. The theme is shared (dark matter as the dual counterpart of each ordinary particle, stated as a heuristic proposal); the duality differs. Under the broad reading of C1 (any dual counterpart of visible matter counts) this would be partial.

relations.label: related
relations.reason: Shares only light, self-interacting dark matter (S13). The self-interactions are short-range (γm exchange and Yukawa-like di-gluino loops) and have no gate in relative velocity. The one velocity dependence, βg/βe (S10), acts between the sectors and suppresses interactions at low velocity: the other place, and the opposite sense, from χ's gate. The dark sector also couples to the SM beyond gravity (βe photons, Higgs/Higgsino portals, sleptonium decays to SM neutrinos), against P4 strict.

relations.label: related
relations.reason: The dark matter is built from magnetically charged partners, but they are elementary point particles with SM masses (MeV for the selectron and light squarks), not topological solitons; 't Hooft–Polyakov enters only as motivation and to set a pole size. The dark matter is the magnetically neutral bound states, and everything lives in ordinary space. There is no localization in momentum, which is what defines the program's form.

relations.label: related
relations.reason: Abundance of many monopole types is asserted (A5, S4, L4; slide 3 also asks 'Why not many monopole types'), not computed. The monopoles are bound, in ordinary space; nothing is in momentum space. With the momentum placement set aside, the abundance half is stated in substance, as it already was in 2012 (item 2).

relations.label: related
relations.reason: Winn explains the monopole null result by confinement, not by placement in conjugate space. Pair-produced poles re-annihilate or dress into neutral monopolium (A4, S11, L10). s-channel production is forbidden by CP and occurs at β≈0. Indirect mass limits are said to rest on an 'Unjustified application of electromagnetic duality' (L17). Light masses make free monopoles hard to find (L9). This mechanism is the second hiding route #11 §11.4 names for the shared-photon form, binding into magnetically neutral composites, though Winn's poles are light, not heavy.

relations.label: partial
relations.reason: A close variant. Every electrically charged SM particle, quarks included, has a magnetically charged partner (S1, S2, A2) under our own photon: Dirac quantization against our e (S5); monopoles couple through the dual tensor of the SM field (L8); electric-origin photons couple to the poles as βg (L6, A3, S10); a γm becomes an ordinary γe after one interaction (S9b). The partners are hidden by binding into magnetically neutral composites (S7, S11, S12), §11.4's second route. Missing: the momentum polarization of the analogs, which is the conjecture's defining clause. Added: spin −½, L↔R exchange, partner masses equal to SM masses. Like §11.4's form, it needs couplings across the sectors that P4 as written excludes. The record does not cite it.

relations.label: related
relations.reason: The magnetic-mirror theme is shared, but the dual sector has no photon of its own: photons are only partitioned by source (S9). The 'effectively dark photons' of A3 are our photons emitted by magnetic charges, a word collision with this form's separate gauge field. The photino is the photon's spin-½ partner, not a gauge boson.

relations.label: not relevant
relations.reason: Dark energy here is a Fermi pressure of massless photinos that weakens as the universe expands (S17); no conjugate universe collapses.

relations.label: not relevant
relations.reason: No clumping in momentum space. Dark matter forms ordinary-space structures (summary p. 5: 'Smatter dominated stars and galaxies' would look dim).

relations.label: not relevant
relations.reason: No long-range attraction among dark particles gated by relative velocity; the dark-dark forces are short-range.

relations.label: collision
relations.reason: 'Reciprocal' (Dirac's e·g = const; A6, S19), 'Dual' (charge duality) and 'polarization' (light polarization, slide 23) collide with the program's Born reciprocity, conjugate and Lagrangian-polarization vocabulary. No Born reciprocity, Fourier or phase-space structure appears.

items.summary:
Winn proposes a 'Dual' to the Standard Model. Each SM particle gets a partner with the same flavor and tree-level mass, spin shifted by ½ ('SUSY-lite'), electric charge e replaced by magnetic charge g (Dirac quantization against our e; squarks −6g/+3g, sleptons and Wino ±2g), chromoelectric charge by chromomagnetic, and SU(2)L by SU(2)R.
- Which photon: ours. Photons are partitioned only by source (γe, γm) and couple across as βg and βe.
- Elementary or solitonic: elementary point particles with SM masses.
- Location: ordinary space. No momentum-space, phase-space, reciprocity or conjugate-variable placement anywhere.
- Dark matter: magnetically and chromomagnetically neutral composites (6 stable neutral smesons, 27 sbaryons, di- and tri-smesons, sleptoniums, 'satoms', 'shatoms', 'smolecules'). They are stable because a ±2g Wino cannot turn −6g into +3g. They self-interact through γm exchange and Yukawa-like di-gluino loops. Abundance is asserted, not computed.
- Monopole searches: pair-produced poles re-annihilate or dress into neutral monopolium (bremsstrahlung, nested light-by-light pairs, Schwinger pairs). s-channel production is CP-forbidden and occurs at β≈0. Indirect limits are said to violate unitarity.
- Dark energy: photino Fermi pressure.
- Coupling to the SM goes beyond gravity: βe photons, the Higgs portal, sleptonium decays.
- Caveats: heuristic; no Lagrangian, interaction terms, manifest Lorentz or gauge invariance, or custodial group; quantitative results need nonperturbative methods.
The critic's quoted 'couple to magnetic particles as g' drops the β that the HTML carries.

items.summary: The 2012 precursor of the 2025 Dual, under the name 'magneto-chiral SUSY' (mcSUSY). The ansatz gives each partner spin shifted by ½, magnetic charge g = n(e/2α) in place of electric charge, chromomagnetic in place of chromoelectric charge, reversed L↔R, the same mass, and no R-parity. It explains the absence of detected monopoles by strong magnetic binding and screening 'similarly to quark hadronization'. It proposes neutral bound partner states and right-handed sneutrino condensates as dark matter, and photinos as dark energy. The partners are elementary and couple to our photon; nothing is placed in momentum space. The two photon classes with βg/βe couplings are not yet in it (0 occurrences of β). Caveats: couplings unspecified; 'a proper analysis of experimental limits' may rule it out. The 2025 draft does not cite it. This record contradicts the critic's 'No arXiv or INSPIRE version found': the model's first public date is 18 June 2012.

items.summary:
The 'extensive paper' the Lepton-Photon summary mentions, as an August 2025 draft, read in full.
- The monopoles are elementary point particles, explicitly not solitons (DR1).
- One electromagnetic potential carries everything (DR5). Photons are labelled by source (DR2). The βg/βe couplings are called 'a conjecture' (DR4), and γm are likened to dark photons 'in a group U (1)e x U (1)m' (DR3).
- Dark matter: neutral shadrons, satoms and smolecules, with their abundance argued qualitatively (DR7, DR18).
- Direct-detection nulls follow from small β and zero weak hypercharge, with a Higgs portal 'beyond simple gravity' (DR10, DR13).
- The monopole null result follows from binding, screening and re-annihilation of light poles, against the usual conclusion that monopoles must be heavy (DR8, DR11).
- No momentum-space, phase-space, reciprocity or conjugate-variable placement.
- Caveats: a toy model without a Lagrangian or controlling symmetry (DR6); a rigorous analysis may rule it out (DR14).
- It cites earlier monopolium-as-dark-matter work (Vento and Traini 2020; Burdyuzha 2018), not Winn's own 2012 paper.

items.summary: The earliest dated public text of the 2025 Dual that I could read; the Aspen talk (item 6) is earlier but known only by its title. It gives right-handed scalar magnetic-monopole partners with charges ±2, ±3, ±6 g (g = e/α) and chromomagnetic squarks. Flavor-changing magnetic currents are forbidden. Confinement and inner bremsstrahlung yield stable neutral 'smesons, sbaryons, di-sleptons'. Photons couple across as beta-g and beta-e, and monopolium is offered as dark matter. Caveat: no gauge invariance or symmetry group 'needed for a proper Lagrangian'. It acknowledges the Aspen Center for Physics. No momentum placement.

overall:
I verified the critic's finding (review/dual-sector/panel/critic.json) from the original files. It holds in its main points, with one wrong claim, one minor correction, and more public versions than it found.

**Confirmed.** Lepton-Photon 2025 contribution 177: talk on 25 Aug 2025, 27 slides, and a 5-page summary (PDF created 10 Nov 2025, uploaded 13 Nov 2025).
- It predates the program's notebook (September 2026), is outside the Minic school, and the record does not cite it. A read-only grep finds Winn only in the critic's file and a workflow script.
- The Dual gives every SM particle a partner: e→g (Dirac quantization against our e), chromoelectric→chromomagnetic, L↔R, spin −½, flavor and mass kept.
- The photon is our own: photons are only labelled by source, and the draft says 'The photon is not affected directly'.
- The monopoles are elementary point particles, not solitons; the draft says so explicitly.
- The charged partners bind into magnetically neutral composites, proposed as self-interacting dark matter and said to evade monopole searches.
- It is heuristic, with no Lagrangian and no manifest Lorentz or gauge invariance.
- No source places anything in momentum space, phase space or a conjugate variable, and none uses Born reciprocity or Fourier structure. This holds for the abstract, both slide decks, the summary, the 40-page draft and the 2012 paper; I read every 'momentum' hit in context by code.

**Wrong in the finding.** 'No arXiv or INSPIRE version found' is wrong. arXiv:1206.4590, 'SUSY Via Magnetic Monopoles and Chirality' by David R. Winn (Fairfield), posted 18 June 2012 (INSPIRE recid 1118961, 0 citations), states the same construction as 'magneto-chiral SUSY':
- 'there are no electrically charged superpartners, only neutral or magnetic charged partners', with g = n(e/2α);
- the absence of detected monopoles is explained by strong magnetic binding and screening;
- neutral 'Smatter' is offered as dark matter that 'likely explain[s] the paucity of signals in underground experiments'.

The model's first public date is therefore 18 June 2012. The two photon classes with βg/βe couplings are new in 2025. The 2025 draft does not cite the 2012 paper.

**Minor correction.** The critic quotes the abstract as 'couple to magnetic particles as g'. The abstract's HTML encodes β before g and e as Symbol-font code point U+F062, and α in 'g=e/α' as U+F061. Browsers and the Book of Abstracts drop these glyphs. The couplings are βg and βe, suppressed at low velocity.

**More public versions, all prior art:**
- Aspen Winter Conference talk, 3 Mar 2025: title only; the slides were refused by a bot check.
- APS Global Physics Summit poster H00.346, 18 Mar 2025: abstract read through the Wayback capture.
- SUSY 2025 talk, 19 Aug 2025: same abstract; its slide 1 links a public 40-page draft dated 17 Aug 2025, which Dropbox still serves and which I read in full.
- Invisibles25 poster, CERN, September 2025: same abstract, no file.
- DPF 2026 talk, 23 July 2026: title and truncated abstract only.

Fairfield's own pages list no publications for him.

**Labels.** All versions agree.
- **C4 shared-photon form: partial.** This is the strongest overlap. Every charged SM particle, quarks included, has a magnetic partner under our own photon, hidden by binding into magnetically neutral composites, which is #11 §11.4's second hiding route. Only the momentum polarization is missing, and it is the conjecture's defining clause. The construction has been public since 2012.
- **C1 identification: related.** Dark matter is the dual of each SM particle, but the duality is electric-magnetic, not phase-space polarization. Under the broad reading of C1 it would be partial.
- **C1 monopole form, C2, C3: related.** Magnetically charged dark matter, abundant many-typed monopoles, and an explanation of the monopole null result, but by binding in ordinary space, with no momentum localization and no solitons.
- **C1 χ form: related**, only through generic light self-interacting dark matter. There is no velocity gate; its β suppression acts between the sectors, at low velocity.
- **C4 separate-photon form: related.** There is no photon of the dual sector. Winn's 'effectively dark photons' and 'U(1)e x U(1)m' are word collisions.
- **C5, C6, C7: not relevant. Hard core:** word collisions only.

**What it means for the record** (my reading):
- Winn leaves the record's 'neither form was found' intact: there is no momentum localization, and the draft rejects solitons.
- C2's 'not found' also stands: his abundance is in ordinary space.
- He adds an uncited and closer instance to C4's 'partly anticipated', public since 2012.
- He gives a second published account of the monopole null result (binding, not placement) beside Khademi 2009.
- His dark sector couples to the SM beyond gravity (Higgs portal, βe photons). That runs against P4 strict, consistent with §11.4's note that the shared-photon form needs P4 restated.

My files are in /home/paul/git/reinholdtsen/conjugate-matter/work/dual-sector/scratch/v-winn/: downloads in dl/, renders in png/, scripts/check_quotes.py, quotes_final.json (72 quotations, all found by code).
